prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 — summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch
- Stick with a “secure future” plan: lower taxes, controlled migration, protected pensions, stronger defence, pragmatic net zero, and community safety. Contrast with Labour as higher tax/spend and weaker on borders/defence.

Economy and tax
- Keep debt falling under fiscal rules; cut bureaucracy (civil service back to pre‑Covid size, halve consultants), boost public sector productivity.
- Halve employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: state pension and a new age‑related tax‑free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation, or 2.5%; protect other pensioner benefits; no new pension taxes.
- Childcare: 30 hours free from 9 months to school; move Child Benefit to a household basis (taper £120k–£160k).
- Raise National Living Wage with earnings; tackle tax avoidance to raise £6bn a year.

Business, infrastructure, innovation and trade
- No rise in corporation tax; maintain full expensing and explore leasing; 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, prompt payment, finance, VAT threshold smoothing).
- Redirect £36bn HS2 savings to regional transport; nationwide contactless rail; automated vehicles; aviation SAF; maritime support; planning and judicial review reforms to speed build‑out.
- R&D to £22bn; compute clusters; advanced manufacturing plan; catapults; City competitiveness (Edinburgh/Mansion House reforms).
- Trade: implement CPTPP; seek FTAs with India/GCC; tough on TCA compliance; protect NHS/food standards.

Welfare and work
- Tighten disability assessments (PIP/WCA), overhaul fit notes, expand mental health support; tougher sanctions after 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; Fraud Bill. Support unpaid carers.

Education and youth
- Advanced British Standard (study broader incl. English/maths to 18); 100,000 extra apprenticeships by closing poor‑outcome degrees; statutory school mobile‑phone ban; parent access to materials; expand SEND places.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 1‑year military (paid, competitive) or civic service (25 days).

Borders, security and foreign policy
- Legal annual cap on migration (work/family), falling yearly; Rwanda removals; rewrite asylum rules; more returns deals; visa health checks, higher fees.
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; 5% R&D plus 2% exploitation; back Ukraine; veterans’ bill/benefits; counter hostile states; restore 0.7% aid when affordable; maintain climate finance.

NHS and social care
- Real‑terms funding rises; 92k more nurses, 28k more doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 extra CDCs.
- Dental recovery (more appointments, NHS service requirement for new dentists).
- £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, replace legacy IT; cut managers by 5,500.
- Women’s Health Strategy; Tobacco & Vapes Bill; implement Cass Review; protect single‑sex care; expand mental health teams in all schools/early hubs.

Crime and justice
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition; Martyn’s Law; hotspot policing, tougher community payback.
- Tougher sentences (domestic murders, sexual/knife crime), 20,000 new prison places by 2030; more deportations of foreign offenders; speed courts; fraud crackdowns.

Energy, net zero and bills
- Annual North Sea licensing; windfall tax to 2028–29; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; CCS clusters; scale nuclear (SMRs, Wylfa); import carbon pricing by 2027.
- Lower/lower‑no new green levies; cap stays; review standing charges; energy‑efficiency vouchers and £6bn for home upgrades; no road pricing or frequent flyer levy.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes: brownfield fast‑track; urban densification; reform nutrient rules with mitigations; regenerate major sites.
- First‑time buyers: permanent higher SDLT threshold (£425k), new Help to Buy, mortgage guarantee.
- Leasehold reform; renters’ reform (end s21 with court changes); CGT relief for landlord-to-tenant sales; protect Green Belt.
- Backing Drivers Bill: no pay‑per‑mile; reverse London ULEZ expansion; referendums for new LTNs/20mph; pavement parking powers; £2 bus fare cap extended.

Equality, rural, environment and Union
- Clarify Equality Act: sex means biological sex; single legal sex; school guidance on gender; cautious on conversion therapy law.
- Farming: +£1bn budget, legal food security target, fast‑track farm infrastructure, tapered seasonal visas; £100m seafood fund; support inshore fleet.
- Water plan (tougher fines, river restoration), flood defences, trees/parks, waste crime penalties, limit new incinerators.
- Strengthen the Union: protect internal market; direct levelling‑up funds to nations; major Scotland/Wales/NI transport and energy commitments; implement Windsor Framework.
